full_judgment:
3. Short facts are that the plaintiffs instituted Partition Suit No. 29 of 1986 in the Court of Munsif (now Assistant Judge), Ghatail, District-Tangail for partition of ejmali property. The suit was decreed ex-parte on 28.09.1989. Thereafter, the defendant-petitioners filed an application under Order IX Rule XIII of the Code of Civil Procedure to set aside the ex-parte decree. On the ground that summons of the original suit was not served upon the defendant and the plaintiff managed a false report of the process server in respect of service of summons and by practicing fraud upon the Court obtained the ex-parte decree in question on 28.09.1989. The application was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 57 of 1989. 

 4. The plaintiff opposite parties entered appearance in the case and filed written objection stating, inter alia, that the summons upon the defendants was duly served by the process server in presence of Mukabela witnesses and as such the petitioner was aware institution of the suit and the date of ex-parte decree. Both the parties adduced evidence in the miscellaneous case and the trial court dismissed the case. On appeal, being Miscellaneous Appeal No. 16 of 1994, the appellate court upon hearing also dismissed the miscellaneous appeal. Thereafter, the petitioner moved the High Court Division in revisional jurisdiction and the High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order discharged the Rule. 

 6. It is not disputed that the Partition Suit No. 29 of 1986 brought by the plaintiff-respondents in the Court of Munsif (now Assistant Judge), Ghatail, District-Tangail was decreed ex-parte on 28.09.1989. It is also not disputed that Miscellaneous Case No. 57 of 1989 under Order IX Rule XIII of the Code of Civil Procedure was brought by defendant-petitioners on the ground of non-service of summons and the same was dismissed by the trial court on the ground of limitation and also on the ground that the defendant Petitioners failed to prove that non service of summons of the original partition suit as alleged by them. 

 7. It is on record in the process server Afzal Hossain who was examined in the miscellaneous case, in his evidence stated that the summons of the original suit was duly served upon the defendant-petitioners. It further appears that P.W.1 son of defendant No.4 who deposed in the miscellaneous case in his evidence stated that summons of the original suit was duly served upon his father that is defendant No.4 of the suit. The trial court and the appellate court concurrently found that the petitioners had failed to prove that summons of the original suit was not served upon them and accordingly dismissed the case.
